title: Parts of the gun
summary: Stock, action, fore-end, barrels, rib and chokes: the names of the main parts of an over-and-under, so you can follow a coach or a gunsmith in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

body.html: Coaches name the parts of the gun all the time, so learn them from the shoulder to the muzzle of an over-and-under, the most common competition gun. The stock goes into the shoulder. Its top edge, where the cheek rests, is the comb; 'raise the comb' or 'drop the comb' is about gun fit. The narrow part held by the trigger hand is the grip, and the rubber pad at the end is the recoil pad.
The stock is made of wood or a composite material. The recoil pad softens the push of the shot, and pads or spacers of different thickness change the length of the stock.

The metal centre of the gun is the receiver or action. On top sits the top lever: push it aside and the gun opens. Behind it is the safety catch, often combined with the barrel selector, which decides which barrel fires first. Underneath is the trigger in its guard.
Inside the receiver sits the firing mechanism. Most competition over-and-unders have a single trigger for both barrels.
A release trigger fires when it is let go, not when it is pressed. Such a gun must carry, as a warning, a sticker with a large 'R' on a fluorescent background on the outer side of the stock.

Under the barrels the other hand holds the fore-end. The barrels have chambers at the back for the cartridges and muzzles at the front, where chokes are screwed in. Along the top runs the rib with a bead at the end. The bead is a reference, not a sight: 'look at the target, not the bead'.

The fore-end also holds the barrels on the action: take it off, and the barrels come off. That is how a gun is taken apart for cleaning and transport. The rib usually has gaps underneath (a 'ventilated rib'), so that heat from the barrels makes the air above it shimmer less. Many guns have a small mid bead halfway along the rib.
Next to the chambers sit the ejectors: when the gun is opened, they throw out the fired cases. Simpler extractors only lift the cases a little, and you take them out by hand.
One safety rule is linked to the parts. After a misfire or any other gun or cartridge failure, the shooter does not open the gun or touch the safety until the referee has looked at it.

notes.html: Two false friends: the 'rib' is the strip along the top of the barrels, and 'break the gun' means open it on its hinge, not damage it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You're seeing too much rib — your head is up.
phrases.meaning: The eye is too high above the rib, usually because the head lifts off the comb.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Check your selector — you fired the top barrel first.
phrases.meaning: The barrel selector is set the wrong way round.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Break your gun and show me it's clear.
phrases.meaning: Open the gun and show empty chambers.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Forget the bead — look at the target.
phrases.meaning: Focus on the target, not on the end of the barrel.

key_points.html: Stock, comb, grip, recoil pad; receiver with top lever, safety and selector; trigger.
Fore-end, barrels with chambers and muzzles, rib with bead.
A release trigger needs an 'R' sticker on the stock.
'Break the gun' means open it; the rib is the strip along the top of the barrels.
After a misfire: do not open the gun or touch the safety before the referee checks.

did_you_know.html: Selective ejectors throw out only a fired case. If you fired one barrel, the unfired cartridge in the other is only lifted a little, so you can take it out calmly by hand.

quiz.q: A coach says 'Raise the comb'. Which part does he mean?

options.text: The top of the stock, where the cheek rests
The small bead at the end of the rib
The choke tube at the muzzle

quiz.explain: The comb is the top of the stock; raising it lifts the eye above the rib.

quiz.q: What must a gun with a release trigger carry?

options.text: A red-painted barrel to warn others
A large 'R' sticker on the stock

quiz.explain: Both rulebooks require the 'R' warning sticker, on a fluorescent background, on the outer side of the buttstock.

quiz.q: What is the barrel selector for?

options.text: To take the barrels off the action
To change the choke in the barrel
To throw the fired cases out
To choose which barrel fires first

quiz.explain: The selector, often combined with the safety, sets the order of the barrels.
